sections.name: Kritter
sections.card:
Summary: The Kremling Krew's foot soldiers. In Donkey Kong 64 they are simply called Kremlings, and they wear a sleeveless leather jacket with a skull-and-crossbones on the back.
Weak points: They are often the weakest Kremlings despite their muscular appearance, and the Prima guide says one hit will send them on their way.
Tips: You meet them on Crocodile Isle and in every world except Fungi Forest and Creepy Castle. In Frantic Factory a red kind belches in a set order, and Lanky has to memorize it and repeat it to earn a Golden Banana.

sections.name: Klump
sections.card:
Summary: A pink Kremling in a yellow-orange vest that throws unripe green oranges at the active Kong and can bounce a Kong backward with its belly.
Weak points: Klumps resist basic attacks, and a direct hit only stuns one for a while. They are truly beaten only by the shockwave attack, a thrown orange, an instrument move, or Chunky touching them in his Hunky Chunky state.
Tips: A beaten Klump salutes, falls over and leaves three oranges. You find them in every level except Frantic Factory, Creepy Castle and the DK Isles hub, and in Fungi Forest only by day, because Skeleton Kremlings take their place at night.

sections.name: Kasplat
sections.card:
Summary: A big, muscular Kremling in a leather jacket and sunglasses that guards a blueprint. It slams the ground to send out a shockwave and can punch a Kong that comes close.
Weak points: Kasplats are tough and often take several hits, but a Kong's shockwave attack or instrument move beats one in a single hit, and so do five oranges. Chunky can flatten one in Hunky Chunky mode, but then it drops no blueprint.
Tips: Its hair colour shows which Kong can take its blueprint (yellow Donkey, red Diddy, blue Lanky, purple Tiny, green Chunky), and the hair turns white once the blueprint is taken. Every level has five Kasplats except Hideout Helm, which has none.

sections.name: Zinger
sections.card:
Summary: A yellow flying enemy. Some Zingers dive-bomb the Kong on sight, and others drop unripe green oranges when they notice you.
Weak points: An orange, an instrument move or a projectile shot defeats a Zinger. The ones that drop oranges generally respawn after you beat them, and the dive-bombers do not.
Tips: They appear on DK Isles and in Jungle Japes, Angry Aztec, Gloomy Galleon, Crystal Caves and, by day only, Fungi Forest, where bats replace them at night. Frantic Factory has robotic Mechanical Zingers instead, and in Angry Aztec a beaten Zinger that falls into the sand burns up and leaves no melon slice.

sections.name: Mad Jack
sections.card:
Summary: The boss of Frantic Factory and the third boss of the game, a giant metallic jack-in-the-box. Tiny Kong fights him on a floor of 16 glowing tiles.
Weak points: Pound the switch on the tile that matches the tile Mad Jack stands on with a Simian Slam to electrocute him, and five hits end the fight. The other switch shocks Tiny instead and costs her half a Watermelon of health.
Tips: While he hops, glide between tiles with Pony Tail Twirl, since he cannot hop diagonally. After the fourth hit he turns invisible, so follow the sparkles he leaves as he jumps. Falling off the stage does not lose the fight: a tile on the lower floor lifts Tiny back.

sections.name: Puftoss
sections.card:
Summary: The boss of Gloomy Galleon, a huge pufferfish. Lanky Kong fights it from a small coconut-half motorboat in a pool, after 250 bananas have been fed to Scoff to open the boss door.
Weak points: Drive the boat through all five DK stars before each one's timer runs out to bring electric poles up from the water, which shock Puftoss. A fifth hit defeats him.
Tips: The star timers start at 30 seconds and shrink to 25, 20, 15 and finally 10 in later rounds. Puftoss cannot hurt Lanky by touching him, but he spits fireballs, and in round two his water slams make shockwaves that vanish when they touch an electric pole.

sections.name: King Kut Out
sections.card:
Summary: The boss of Creepy Castle and the seventh, next-to-last boss of the game: a crude cardboard cut-out of King K. Rool worked by two Kritters, fought in an arena walled by a castle rampart, in the rain.
Weak points: Step into the Barrel Cannon that faces it and blast into it. The ninth hit destroys it and the Boss Key drops in the middle of the arena.
Tips: A shot with bad timing blasts the Kong out of the arena for good, and the next Kong comes out of the Tag Barrel (by default Tiny, then Chunky, Donkey and Diddy after Lanky). After the third hit a darker decoy follows it from the opposite wall, and blasting at the decoy throws you out. After three more hits it moves faster, so fire just as it appears in front of you; the ghosts that spawn near the cannons can be beaten to regain health.

sections.name: Golden Banana
sections.card:
Summary: Donkey Kong's own supply of bananas from his hoard, which the Kremlings steal and the Kongs have to recover. There are 200 in the seven worlds and DK Isles, plus a hidden 201st.
Uses: B. Locker keeps you out of the other worlds until you carry a minimum number of Golden Bananas, a different number for each world. Snide also pays one for every blueprint you bring him.
Tips: Each Kong has to collect five in every world by finishing their own tasks, 25 per world in all. The hidden 201st is larger and carries the Rare logo, and all 201 are needed for 101 percent and the second ending.

sections.name: Blueprint
sections.card:
Summary: The design plans for the Blast-o-Matic, which the Kongs recover for Snide. There are 40 in all, five in every area except Hideout Helm, one for each Kong.
Uses: Each Kong takes their blueprints to Snide's H.Q. and gets a Golden Banana for every one. In Hideout Helm each blueprint also delays the Blast-o-Matic's countdown by a minute.
Tips: Every blueprint is guarded by a Kasplat whose hair colour matches the Kong who can take it, and the wrong Kong sees only a hologram. The Helm countdown starts at ten minutes and can reach 50 with all 40, and once you have recovered them all Snide lets you replay most of the bonus stages.
